nodes.name: Drop-cast RuO₂ on FTO
nodes.procedure: RuO₂ was synthesized by drop-casting 35 μl of aqueous RuCl₃ solution (20 mmol l⁻¹) onto fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrate with an area of 1 × 1 cm² heated at 70 °C on a hot plate. After the solution was dried, the FTO substrate coated with RuCl₃ was moved into a muffle furnace and annealed at 500 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: Typically, RuO₂ was synthesized by drop-casting 35 μl of aqueous RuCl₃ solution (20 mmol l⁻¹) onto fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrate... annealed at 500 °C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Modified RuO₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: For the modified RuO₂ (denoted as m-RuO₂), the same concentration of RuCl₃ (20 mmol l⁻¹, 35 μl) was used with NaCl added at Ru:Na molar ratio of 1:3. Drop-cast onto FTO substrate (1×1 cm²) heated at 70 °C on hot plate. After drying, annealed in muffle furnace at 500 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: For the modified RuO₂ with N₂Φ⁺ (denoted as m-RuO₂), the same concentration of RuCl₃ was used, but a certain amount of NaCl was added. After optimization, the sample synthesized with a molar ratio of Ru:Na = 1:3... all the m-RuO₂ catalysts studied in this work were prepared under the optimized condition.

nodes.name: Low-temp RuO₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: RuO₂ sample with lower crystallinity and more defects was synthesized at 300 °C using the same drop-casting procedure of 35 μl RuCl₃ solution (20 mmol l⁻¹) onto FTO substrate heated at 70 °C, followed by annealing at 300 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: RuO₂ sample with lower crystallinity and more defects was also synthesized at 300 °C, denoted as RuO₂(300°C).

nodes.name: Au deposition on RuO₂
nodes.procedure: Au was deposited onto RuO₂ to yield Au/RuO₂ using magnetic sputtering (temperature was set at 100 °C for 1 min).
nodes.source_text: Au was deposited onto RuO₂ to yield Au/RuO₂ using magnetic sputtering (temperature was set at 100 °C for 1 min).

nodes.name: IrO₂ synthesis on FTO
nodes.procedure: For the Ir oxide-based catalysts (IrO₂, m-IrO₂ and Co-IrO₂), the synthesis conditions were similar to RuO₂ synthesis, but RuCl₃ was replaced by IrCl₃ (20 mmol l⁻¹ aqueous IrCl₃ solution, 35 μl drop-cast onto FTO substrate heated at 70 °C, dried, then annealed at 500 °C for 2 h).
nodes.source_text: For the Ir oxide-based catalysts (IrO₂, m·IrO₂ and Co·IrO₂), the synthesis conditions were similar, but RuCl₃ was replaced by IrCl₃ (20 mmol l⁻¹ aqueous IrCl₃ solution, 35 μl).

nodes.name: PLD oxide synthesis
nodes.procedure: TiO₂, Co₃O₄, WO₃ and SrIrO₃ were synthesized on FTO using pulsed laser deposition (PLD). Detailed parameter settings for PLD are summarized in Supplementary Table 1.
nodes.source_text: These oxides were synthesized on FTO using pulsed laser deposition (PLD).

nodes.name: Electrochemical deposition of metal hydroxides
nodes.procedure: The metal hydroxides used to study the OER reaction kinetics in alkaline medium were synthesized by electrochemical deposition. Co, CoFe and CoNi hydroxides were synthesized by following the procedure described in our recent work, except that the solutions for CoFe and CoNi were changed to those with 10 at.% of Fe and 25 at.% of Ni, respectively. Ni and NiFe hydroxides were synthesized by anodic electrochemical deposition according to the paper by Trotochaud et al.
nodes.source_text: The metal hydroxides used to study the OER reaction kinetics in alkaline medium were synthesized by electrochemical deposition.

Unmodified RuO2 with a well-defined crystalline rutile structure shows TafIE in acidic electrolyte, however, when the structure of RuO2 is modified with more defects and local lattice distortion (denoted as m-RuO2), TafIE is absent for acidic OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows RuO2 stable with no notable bulk structure change but surface rearrangement by peak shift in acidic H/D electrolytes; m-RuO2 exhibits blue shift consistent with shorter Ru-O bonds from XAS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman spectroscopy (Fig. 4g,h...) reveals that ${ \mathrm { R u O } } _ { 2 }$ is stable with no notable bulk structure change... A blue shift in Raman peaks is seen in $m { \cdot } \mathrm { R u O } _ { 2 }$ (Fig. 4h), consistent with the shorter Ru–O bonds revealed by XAS results.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FT-IR reveals evolution of oxide (*OH, *O, *OO, *OOH) and superoxide species at 1.0–1.8 V vs RHE/RDE on RuO2 and m-RuO2; O-D vibration red-shifted vs O-H; peaks 1000-1250 cm⁻¹ attributed to surface oxide/superoxide species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ FT-IR spectroscopy (Fig. 4i...) further reveals that H/D isotope substitution affects the adsorbed species... three peaks emerging in the range of 1000-1250 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the oxide and superoxide species generated at the catalyst surface.
